title: Named keyword Quagmire alphabets on LP2
question: Do the source's named keyword alphabets and six key distributions produce LP2's whole-book rune frequencies?
reader_question: Do named keyword alphabets fit LP2's rune frequencies?
summary: Exact Stage V replay checks 68 named alphabets in all source-defined triples against six key-value distributions. No combination reaches the source's positive-lead threshold.
finding: The source calibration gate passes and there are no +10 leads. Four key distributions have all 314,432 combinations both control-powered and below the source's −10 exclusion cutoff. Hexadecimal digits leave 135 powered non-exclusions; uniform A–Z leaves 10,197, while 272,640 A–Z combinations lack power. No plaintext or key is recovered.
limitations: This is a unigram frequency screen of fixed named alphabets and independent key-value distributions, not a decryption. It does not test arbitrary keywords, actual key order, alternative boundaries, non-independent keys or layered ciphers. Raw source exclusions must not be confused with control-powered exclusions.
next_steps: A surviving proposal needs a specific keyword, key sequence and a prediction of rune order or plaintext beyond the observed frequency profile.

scope.representation: Canonical GP29 LP2-00–55 stream represented by its pooled 12,956-rune frequency vector.
scope.procedure: Rerun pinned Stage V's G1 same-family model controls and G2 flat-key power screen, then audit all source family summaries and listed survivors. Independently reconstruct the site manuscript rune vector.
scope.parameters: 34 source-specified keywords yield 68 distinct alphabets including identity and inverse forms. All 68^3 alphabet triples for each of six key-value distributions, maximizing over three sign modes and 29 offsets; −10 exclusion, +10 lead, and at least 18/20 G2 flat-key exclusions for power.
scope.exclusions: Other keywords or alphabet constructions, dependent or ordered keys, page-specific resets, alternate statistics and sequence-level decryption.

review.kind: exact public-source Stage V replay with independent manuscript and verdict audit
review.reviewer: Pinned source result reproduced byte-for-byte over 10,357 rows; all G1/G2 family and survivor verdicts audited; site pages independently reproduce the 29-rune input counts

reproduction.environment: Bundled checks use Python 3 standard library. Optional full source replay requires NumPy and a pinned external checkout.

visuals.caption: Control-qualified outcomes for six key-value distributions. Each bar represents 314,432 alphabet combinations within one bounded screen; tiny hex survivors are listed exactly in the article.
